name: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

criteria.description: Coronary angiography demonstrating non-traumatic coronary artery wall dissection or intramural hematoma
No evidence of atherosclerotic coronary artery disease on imaging
Presentation with acute coronary syndrome symptoms such as chest pain or myocardial infarction
Exclusion of traumatic or iatrogenic causes of coronary artery dissection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Angiographic evidence of coronary artery dissection without atherosclerosis and exclusion of traumatic or iatrogenic causes in a patient presenting with acute coronary syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on coronary angiography; intravascular imaging (OCT or IVUS) may aid in confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute chest pain consistent with myocardial ischemia
searchTerms: pain from heart blood flow blockage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electrocardiographic changes indicative of acute coronary syndrome
searchTerms: signs of acute coronary event on ECG

common.symptomName: Radiating chest pain to left arm or jaw
searchTerms: chest pain spreading to arm or jaw
heart pain moving to left arm or jaw

imaging: Coronary angiography showing coronary artery dissection or intramural hematoma
Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirming arterial wall separation
Echocardiography may show regional wall motion abnormalities
genetic: Association with connective tissue disorders (e.g., fibromuscular dysplasia) in some cases
other: Exclusion of atherosclerotic disease and traumatic causes is essential

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Risk factors such as hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking
Absence of arterial wall dissection on angiography
Sudden occlusion without arterial wall abnormalities

references: Saw J. Spontaneous coronary artery dissection. Can J Cardiol. 2013;29(9):1027-1033.
Tweet MS, Hayes SN, Pitta SR, et al. Clinical features, management, and prognosis of spontaneous coronary artery dissection. Circulation. 2012;126(5):579-588.
Hayes SN, Kim ESH, Saw J, et al. Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: Current State of the Science: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2018;137(19):e523-e557.
